digests.lede: Polymarket's dated markets price H100 rent at $2.14 an hour for December 2028. Banks are preparing to sell $4.5B of GPU-backed loans tied to CoreWeave, whose 2031 bonds yield about 18%. Lenders are also selling AI data center loans, some well below face value. Silicon Data reads the autumn rise in GPU rent as a neocloud credit squeeze.

items.t: Polymarket opened H100 perpetuals. They are cash-settled, never expire and track a 24-hour average of Ornn's H100 SXM index. Leverage is 3x up to $500K notional, 2x to $1M and 1x above. B200 and B300 perpetuals are scheduled for 27 Nov.

The H100 perpetual read $3.175 at 08:20 Lisbon, up 2.8% in 24 hours. Volume was $572,994 in 24 hours. Open interest was $37,275, small against volume. A digest reported first-day volume of about $1.97M and open interest of about $25.7K.
Shayne Coplan says the H100 perpetuals trade at spreads under one cent.
Stanley He counts about ten compute derivatives markets launching before any working spot market. All settle on index prices that he calls a black box.
Compute Exchange runs a two-sided sealed-bid auction at GTC DC on 2 Dec. Each lot is one 8-GPU B200 or B300 node in a US data center. The term is 12 months from 1 Apr 2027, with 99.5% monthly uptime.
Architect's AX exchange lists futures on H100, H200, B200 and B300 rental prices. NautilusTrader shipped an adapter to trade them.
Ornn launched a Contract Index. It prices H100, B200 and B300 capacity from signed long-term contracts, not from listings.
Polymarket launched cash-settled markets on H100, B200 and B300 rent out to 2028. They settle on Ornn's indexes.
Kenton Prescott compares Polymarket's B300 rental markets with an ideal swap contract.
Carmen Li argues the new US remote-access curbs could move different parts of the compute forward curve in different ways.
CME compute futures still await regulatory review, Carmen Li says. They are not trading yet.
Compute Exchange promoted its B200 and B300 auction at GTC DC.

Polymarket's dated H100 markets priced rent at $3.04 an hour for December 2026. December 2027 sat at $2.71. December 2028 sat at $2.14. Ornn settled H100 SXM at $3.10 on 25 Nov. December 2026 H100 contracts traded about $501,000.
Allium says Polymarket's GPU rental markets traded $4.1M in their first three days. By its count, H100 drew $1.93M. B200 drew $1.13M and B300 drew $1.08M.

Silicon Data: B200 spot rose 28% from 29 May to 24 Nov. Its two-year discount to spot widened from 7.9% to 18.1%. H100 term rates rose 16% to 22% at every length. Steve Hou reads this as a neocloud credit squeeze. He says the B300's arrival could cause the same B200 shape.
Silicon Data says CoreWeave's 30% to 50% increases on new contracts match the year-on-year rise in its on-demand rates.
SemiAnalysis measured 2.28x better performance per dollar for Amazon's Trainium3 UltraServer than for Nvidia's GB300 NVL72 on its agentic inference benchmark.

GPU Rental Prices puts the typical on-demand H100 at $3.51 an hour for November to date. That is 6.5% above October's $3.30. B200 rose 8.9% to $8.42. B300 rose 11.7% to $10.28. On the same offers in both months, H100 rose 2.8%.
P Equity Research posted a J.P. Morgan note on GPU rents. It says H100 averaged $3.03 an hour in November. That is up 6.7% on October. A100 averaged $1.61, up 4.4%.

items.t: Space Investor says SpaceX is cutting its rent for Blackwell GPUs. The post cites an unpublished SemiAnalysis client note. It claims small-cluster B200 and B300 spot rates fell to $10 to $12 an hour, from about $15.
items.src: Space Investor on X, citing SemiAnalysis

items.t: Two unnamed insiders say chip sellers warned neoclouds against renting capacity to Chinese firms. The sellers threatened to withhold Nvidia supply. A US rule on remote chip access took effect on 19 Nov. The report says spare Asian capacity is moving to US and European markets. It says this shift is pushing rents down.
Lenders paused billions of dollars in data center loans tied to ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent after the new US chip-access curbs. Banks struggle to sell down their exposure.
A post citing JPMorgan research ties about $456B of data center financing to six companies: Amazon and Oracle about $117B each, Meta $81B, Google $74B, Microsoft $34B, Nvidia $33B.

Morgan Stanley and MUFG are preparing to sell $4.5B of CoreWeave-related loans. GPUs serving Meta data center projects back the loans. Talk points to an investment-grade rating and a 7% to 7.5% yield. Terms are not final.

CoreWeave's 2031 bonds yield about 18%. Credit default swap prices imply more than a 70% chance of default within five years. CoreWeave stock closed at $42.57 on 25 Nov. It fell 11% over five sessions.

Banks are selling AI data center loans as construction risks grow. HSBC sold about $300M of an $18B Project Jupiter loan package at prices in the mid-80s. ING offered about $500M of data center loans. Societe Generale is seeking buyers for $300M of Oracle-related project debt.
